playerTip: Defensive Win Shares (DWS) is an all-in-one metric originally developed by Bill James for baseball, and adapted by Justin Kubatko (basketball-reference) for use in basketball. DWS attempts to divvy up credit for team success on defense to the individuals on the team, by estimating the number of defensive possessions a player was involved in over the year and the number of points prevented by the player's defensive efforts, which are then converted into the number of wins the player has contributed to their team. DWS is computed using box score statistics only, and therefore does not account for who the player is playing with or against. The equation for DWS can be found at https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/about/ws.html

playerTip: Value Point System (VPS) is an all-in-one metric developed by Hall of Fame Coach Danny Miles. In Miles' words, VPS provides an all-encompassing look at how players and teams perform by weighing their positive contributions against their negative ones - the resulting number shows how effective the player is. A VPS of 1 is considered average, while anything north of 2 is elite. VPS  is computed using box score statistics only, and therefore does not account for who the player is playing with or against. The equation for VPS can be found at https://team.fastmodelsports.com/2017/08/21/dna-stat-value-point-system/

playerTip: Wins Above Replacement Player (WARP) is an all-in-one metric developed by Kevin Pelton. In Pelton's words, WARP seeks to evaluate players in the context of a team made up of them and four completely average players. The performance of this team is then compared to that of a team made up of four average players and one replacement-level player. WARP is computed using box score statistics only, and therefore does not account for who the player is playing with or against. The equation for WARP can be found at https://sonicscentral.com/warp.html
